To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination of infrared intensity with histogram of gradient orientations and local binary patterns, approximated on multiple scales, is a promising approach to pedestrian detection in infrared images.

(i) the combination of four channels, namely infrared intensity, normalized gradient magnitude, histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) and local binary patterns (LBP) is effective for far infrared pedestrian detection, (ii) the combination of multiple scale feature approximation with the use of morphological based region proposals is an effective strategy for fast infrared pedestrian detection, and (iii) uniform LBP patterns perform better than rotation invariant ones for infrared pedestrian detection.

the use of infrared, gradient, gradient magnitude and local binar patterns features, with multiple scale approximated feature computation and a morphological based region proposal generation algorithm, is a viable approach for pedestrian detection in infrared images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of pedestrians in far infrared images.
the development of pedestrian detection algorithms that can be used in night vision applications for autonomous cars, surveillance systems and other security applications.
the development of an infrared pedestrian detector for night vision applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is fast, robust and accurate.
the combination of multiple features and the use of feature approximation for multiple scale computation results in a fast and accurate detector.
the proposed method is a good trade off between speed and accuracy for pedestrian detection in infrared images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of multiple features in the proposed way can boost detection accuracy and speed for far infrared images.
the proposed method is a good trade-off between execution time, accuracy and robustness.

we have ported a popular monocular pedestrian detection approach to the infrared domain, we have combined multiple channel features and we have proposed a novel approach for multiple scale feature computation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method is able to achieve a reasonable detection speed while maintaining the accuracy.
the combination of multiple feature channels and multiple scales approximation can boost detection accuracy and speed in the infrared domain.
a pedestrian detection system in the far infrared domain is possible.
